text:
Email thread "Alpha Lexington" (Gmail thread 1a0d4b73ef31138e). Message bodies verbatim (typographic quotes normalised to straight); signatures omitted.

From: J.C. Fischer <jc.fischer@trilogy.com>, EVP Operations, 2 Hour Learning
Date: 2026-10-01 09:20 PT
To: Matt Barge; cc Yash Chitneni, Robbie Forrest, Arthur

Hey y'all,

Lexington's lawyers sent us a note with more specific request than the changes we already made. The following changes should be made so our counsel can respond that we have addressed their concerns:

"Alpha in Greater Boston

Looking for a private school your child can't wait to go to each morning? Alpha's mastery-based, AI-driven approach lets students complete their academics in two hours. Alpha classes rank in the top 1% nationally.

The rest of the day is spent on life skills and team-based workshops that build motivation and teach leadership, grit, financial literacy, and entrepreneurship.

At Alpha, kids love school. We're not just preparing students for tests; we're preparing them for limitless futures.

Alpha operates two campuses in Greater Boston today: Alpha Beacon Hill and Alpha Jamaica Plain. Both are open for enrollment.

Proposed Lexington campus

Alpha has proposed a campus in Lexington, Massachusetts. The proposal is under review by the Lexington School Committee and has not been approved. No Lexington campus is open, and Alpha is not enrolling students for a Lexington location. We will update this page if and when the School Committee takes action.

Families in the Lexington area who want to learn about Alpha can visit Alpha Beacon Hill or Alpha Jamaica Plain."

Can you confirm when the change has been made?

Thank you,

From: J.C. Fischer <jc.fischer@trilogy.com>
Date: 2026-10-02 11:53 PT
To: Matt Barge; cc Rachel Goodlad, Jeremy Williams, Yash Chitneni, Robbie Forrest, Arthur

Thanks y'all. Counsel replied:

I would remove the line "K-8 Private School in Boston, MA" from the header
to avoid any implications that there's an active school (also, that
statement will never be accurate even when open – Boston is 20 miles from
Lexington!)

On the text in the body, I would replace "not been approved" with "not yet
received approval" – the former could imply it was (or is expected to be)
rejected, and I don't think you need to go that far.

Also, instead of the last line, do you want to elaborate a bit with
something like "Alpha welcomes inquiries from interested families, and will
update this page if and when the School Committee takes action"? Perhaps
with a hyperlink on the "welcomes inquiries" to the stay-in-the-know popup?
I presume that you want to have a bullpen of interested families ready to
go once Lexington approves, and I think that's a reasonable position to
take at present on the website.

Thank you,
